<objective>
Replace the two hand-rolled `setTimeout(..., 100)` auto-save suppression windows with a single service-owned `applyDefaults(apply)` API whose window closes deterministically (D-08).

Purpose: RACE-02's second half. `ModelAttachmentDefaultsService.setupAutoSave` gates its persistence stream on `filter(() => !this.isApplyingDefaults)`. Two callers — `compare-modal.component.ts:220,235` and `comparison-panel.component.ts:375,396` — raise that flag, apply overlays, then lower it after a 100ms guess. 100ms is not derived from anything: if it is too short the app persists defaults it was told to skip; if the flag is ever left raised, auto-save stops silently. The service, which owns the guard, should own when the window closes.

Output: an `applyDefaults(apply: () => void)` API using a microtask-bounded window, both call sites migrated, the raw setter removed, and tests that pin the window with `fakeAsync`/`tick(0)` rather than wall-clock timing.
</objective>

  <behavior>
    - Inside the callback passed to `applyDefaults`, the suppression flag reads as raised.
    - Immediately after `applyDefaults` returns (same synchronous turn), the flag still reads as raised — the window has not closed yet.
    - After the microtask queue drains (`tick(0)` under `fakeAsync`), the flag reads as lowered.
    - If the callback throws, the exception propagates to the caller AND the flag is still lowered after the microtask drain — the window can never get stuck open.
    - Calling `applyDefaults` twice in a row leaves the flag lowered after the drain.
  </behavior>
  <action>
Add a service-owned suppression window to `ModelAttachmentDefaultsService`.

<!-- planner-discipline-allow: setApplyingDefaults -->

Add `applyDefaults(apply: () => void): void` positioned where `setApplyingDefaults` currently sits
(~line 233). Implementation: set `this.isApplyingDefaults = true`; run `apply()` inside a `try`; in the
`finally` block, schedule the flag's clear with `queueMicrotask(() => { this.isApplyingDefaults = false; })`.

Why a microtask and not a timer: `StateManagementService`'s `BehaviorSubject.next()` notifies its
subscribers SYNCHRONOUSLY, and every mutation the callback performs (`addOverlayToLeftPanel`,
`addOverlayToRightPanel`, `updateOverlayScale`) goes through that subject. By the time `apply()` returns,
`setupAutoSave`'s `map` → `distinctUntilChanged` → `filter(() => !this.isApplyingDefaults)` stages have
already run for each of those emissions — only the terminal `debounceTime(500)` is asynchronous, and it
sits AFTER the guard. A microtask deferral therefore closes the window at the first moment it is provably
safe, with no guessed duration. Put that reasoning in a JSDoc block above the method (explaining WHY,
per this repo's comment convention), including the note that the `finally` placement is what guarantees
the flag clears even when `apply()` throws.

Delete `setApplyingDefaults` entirely once both call sites are migrated in Task 2 — D-08 states both
callers move to the new API, so the raw setter has no remaining consumer and leaving it would let a future
caller reintroduce the stuck-flag failure mode. (Sequencing note: make this deletion part of THIS task's
edit but run the task's verify only after Task 2's call-site migration, or perform Task 2's call-site
edits first and delete the setter last — either order is fine as long as the plan's final commit compiles.)

Leave `setupAutoSave`, `panelDataEqual`, `saveOverlaysForModel`, `getOverlaysForModel`,
`hasDefaultsForModel`, and the localStorage/IndexedDB persistence paths untouched. Per
`.claude/skills/attachment-system/SKILL.md`, overlay identity and `sourceAttachmentPointId` semantics are
invariants — this change alters only WHEN the auto-save guard lowers, never what is saved.

In `model-attachment-defaults.service.spec.ts`, replace the `describe('setApplyingDefaults')` block
(lines 286-292) with a `describe('applyDefaults')` block covering every case in this task's `<behavior>`
list. Use `fakeAsync` + `tick(0)` (both already imported at line 1) to drive the microtask boundary —
never assert on wall-clock timing. Read the private flag through
`(service as unknown as Record<string, unknown>)['isApplyingDefaults']`. Include the throwing-callback
case with `expect(() => service.applyDefaults(() => { throw new Error('boom'); })).toThrow()` followed by
a `tick(0)` and a flag assertion.
  </action>

## Trust Boundaries

| Boundary | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| default-overlay application → persistence stream | A bulk state mutation crosses a guard that decides whether it is persisted back as the user's saved defaults |

## STRIDE Threat Register

| Threat ID | Category | Component | Severity | Disposition | Mitigation Plan |
|-----------|----------|-----------|----------|-------------|-----------------|
| T-03-14 | Tampering | auto-save persisting overlays it was told to skip because the 100ms window closed early | medium | mitigate | Window is bounded by the microtask queue, which provably drains after every synchronous `BehaviorSubject.next()` the callback triggers; verified by a `fakeAsync`/`tick(0)` test rather than assumed. |
| T-03-15 | Denial of Service | suppression flag left raised, silently disabling auto-save for the session | medium | mitigate | The clear is scheduled from a `finally` block so it runs even when the callback throws; a spec asserts the throwing path lowers the flag. Removing the raw setter prevents a future caller from raising the flag without scheduling a clear. |
| T-03-SC | Tampering | npm/pip/cargo installs | high | accept | No packages installed; `queueMicrotask` is a native platform API. |
</threat_model>
